sample-1109-1: My family has hunted and fished this coast for four generations. This bill wouldn't make anyone safer — it would make ordinary gear a crime and turn law-abiding neighbors into suspects. Lewiston broke all our hearts, but the answer is enforcement of the laws we have, not new ones aimed at the wrong people.
sample-1109-2: I was two blocks from Schemengees that night. I am asking the committee to remember that the difference between a tragedy and a catastrophe was measured in how many rounds fit in a magazine. No hunter I know needs thirty rounds. Please pass this bill.
sample-1109-3: I'm a sportsman and a veteran. The devices this bill bans are standard equipment sold for decades. Grandfathering language or not, this makes criminals out of people who've done nothing wrong. Focus on the yellow flag law and mental health beds instead.
sample-1109-4: As an emergency physician I treat what these devices do. The wound patterns from high-capacity sustained fire are simply different, and survivability drops with every additional round fired. This is a public health measure, and the evidence from other states supports it.
